glance_takeaway: A blameless post-incident review of a June 24 SEV-1 partial outage of ledgerline's invoicing API (14:02-18:19 UTC, 4h17m), where a bad deploy (a search rewrite to a leading-wildcard LIKE that abandoned its index) combined with two pre-existing latent weaknesses - autovacuum debt / table bloat from a June 22 backfill, and jitterless 1s client retries saturating a shared 80-connection pool - to turn a one-endpoint regression into a platform-wide outage. Key numbers legible at a glance: 31.2% peak error rate, 2,312 orgs affected, ~$41,300 SLA credits, ~362,000 failed requests, zero data loss. Four headline cards land the synthesis: no single root cause; 68 minutes lost to diagnosis (wrong network theory; alerts watched error rate not latency, dashboards sampled 1/100); rollback was impossible (migration irreversibly dropped the old index, ~6h rebuild) so a feature flag stopped the bleeding at 17:05; and three P0 fixes are scheduled for Q3 2026, one per failure leg.

F2.note: Stat row + impact table: '19.1% average across the window; peak 31.2% at 15:47'; '≈362,000 of ≈1.9 M requests'

F4.note: Stat row + table: '2,312 organizations — 24.4% of 9,480 active'; '≈$41,300 across 216 enterprise contracts'; zero data loss; '37,400 queued deliveries, all replayed by 19:05'

F6.note: Cause card 1: 'canary table holds ~2 M rows, where the same scan takes ~180 ms — under every alert threshold'

F7.note: Cause card 2: June 22 backfill, 38.1 M dead tuples, 190 GB → 213 GB (12.2% bloat), threshold '≈54.9 M dead tuples' on a 274.2 M-row table; 'Autovacuum never ran — correctly, by its configuration'

F8.note: Cause card 2 evidence box: bloat-free ~26 s vs observed 24-31 s 'straddling the 30-second statement timeout'; '~57% of search queries were killed'; 'A killed query still held its pooled connection for the full 30 s'

F9.note: Cause card 3 + pool bars: pgbouncer pool of 80 shared by reads/writes/PDF/webhooks; '≈1.2/s → ≈5.6/s: demand ≈160+ vs 80 — saturation at 15:12'; 'peak 1,437 waiting clients at 15:58'

F10.note: Cause card 3: 'fixed 1-second interval, 3 attempts, no jitter, no retry budget... 3,200 → 15,020 rpm (4.7×)... extra load, zero extra successes... nearly two hours'; pool bump 80→200 at 16:20 backfired, reverted 16:31

F11.note: Takeaway card 2, gaps grid, timeline: 14:05 advisory + 504s + broken deploy markers anchored a network hypothesis 14:20-15:10 (50 min); first alert 14:11 to diagnosis 15:19 = 68 min

F12.note: Rollback section: migration 0412 'dropped idx_invoices_org_number'; 'Code rollback wouldn't help... would seq-scan just the same'; rebuild ~6 h, 'started at 16:05... finished at 21:48 — well after incident close'

F13.note: Rollback section + timeline: 16:35 staging verification of the exact-match fallback on the untouched unique index; invoice_search_contains to 0% at 17:05; errors <3% within ten minutes; 'the flip took 90 seconds'; exact-match-only until re-enable June 26

F14.note: Rollback section + timeline: VACUUM (ANALYZE) 17:12-17:50 removed the 38.1 M dead tuples and refreshed statistics; SLOs met from 17:53; closed 18:19 after 26 minutes of stable metrics

F15.note: Gaps grid: only firing alert 'gateway 5xx > 2% over 5 min' (14:11); no latency SLO alert for invoicing despite p99 exploding 14:07; sampling 1/100 ('~0.7 samples per minute'); deploy marker broken since June 10 hid the 14:02 deploy

F16.note: Remediation table: 9 items, 3 P0 / 3 P1 / 3 P2, named owners and quarters; P0s all Q3 2026 (Priya N. latency SLO alerts, Marcus T. pgbouncer saturation + isolation, Dana K. retries with backoff/full jitter/budgets); P1s include migration-reversibility policy, autovacuum tuning, CI query-plan checks
